description: haiccing's packages, as the development tool (tools/package-writer) writes them: each self-contained (no requires), in the package structure (notes/packages.md). modules: ours it starts from (and its swarms' modules.json); with: other definitions' modules, written in with it (this tool's convenience); the hand-written parts from haiccing/<repo>/.

mycelium.description: The repository layer: layered git repositories (mycelium-git, -layer, -repo), topics, URIs and paths; with p2p-git, git on Hyperdrive, which mycelium-git runs on. Code only: published for development.

haicc.description: HAICC, the platform: its boot (haicc-base-boot), declaring and reconciling (haicc-reconcile), the lifecycle (haicc-deployment) and the package manager (pkgm-base-manager). The entry: everything starts here.
readme: Linux on x86-64 (on Windows: inside WSL2), with `curl` and `tar`. The setup is this package's release, `haicc-setup.sh`; one command, stopping at the first step that fails:

The boot runs in two stages. Stage 1, `./boot`, in plain shell: Linux x86-64 and Node.js (Node.js fixed with your yes, into `nodejs/`); HAICC's package copied whole into `packages/base-package-haicc/`; `./haicc` written. Stage 2, `./haicc boot`: the host's other prerequisites (git 2.25 or later; Docker Engine installed, running, rootful, native, and you in the `docker` group), each fixed only with your yes (`--yes` agrees beforehand); then `haiccing/install` if there (one `./haicc` command a line), or the next commands.

Everything it does is logged in the work folder's `log/` (`~/haicc-work/log/`): files named by their start, newest last. Everything is in plain sight: `boot`, `shutdown`, `haicc`, `haiccing/`, `packages/`, `nodejs/`, `log/`; no hidden folders. `./shutdown` takes it all back to the setup (keeping `haiccing/`, `log/`, `nodejs/`); `./boot` again sets it up.

The rest of HAICC (`haicc-reconcile`, `haicc-deployment`) runs in the nodes: `./haicc boot <swarm>` makes a swarm (in `swarms.json`), `<swarm>/haicc boot <node>` a node in it (in `<swarm>/nodes.json`; the first is the master), with its own HAICC and package manager. `haicc boot` and `haicc shutdown` work on the config of the folder they are called from.

pkgm.description: The package manager: a swarm's codebase assembled from a package into its master's package repository; a package's tests, bottom up. Node's built-ins only. (Published for development; the platform carries it.)
readme: Into each swarm node's manager (`<swarm>/<node>/packages/`), copied in whole by the root's `./haicc boot <swarm>/<node>`; not at the root, which runs HAICC alone.

p2p.description: The p2p substrate, ours: store, discovery, connections, replication, channels, repositories on Hypercore, the name service, the node and its managers. Code only: published for development.

splectral.description: The Splectral platform: the server, its shell, the contract and model, transports, and the extensions for p2p swarms (watchers, actions, observer), scenarios, the timeline and replay; the map view (splectral/base-view-map), shared by the demos. Code only: published for development.

demo-liveness.description: Demo project: A node goes quiet. Its project (project.json) and its Splectral component (splectral/base-demo-liveness).

demo-other-host.description: Demo project: A node on another host. Its project (project.json) and its Splectral component (splectral/base-demo-other-host).

swarm-three-nodes.description: A configured swarm, no application: a master and two nodes on one host, the p2p node as its codebase.
